newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's most wanted guerrilla stands trial.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's most wanted guerrilla stands trial.

text.p: Argentine guerrilla Enrique Gorriaran Merlo, who is blamed for the killing of Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza, stood trial on Thursday in connection with the 1989 attack on the Argentine army barracks of La Tablada.

The bald, bearded 55-year-old and his ex-wife, Ana Sivori, shouted defiantly before a prosecutor began reading out 300 pages of charges for Argentina's last major guerrilla attack, in which 39 people died, 60 were wounded and three went missing.
Gorriaran Merlo, who was arrested after years on the run while walking along a street in Mexico in 1995, faces a life sentence, as does his former wife.
His defence will argue that he was detained with the help of Argentine secret services, which was illegal.

"The Argentine government, together with Mexico, kidnapped me," the former Marxist leader of the People's Revolutionary Army (ERP) and All for the Fatherland Movement (MTP) told reporters at a heavily-guarded court outside Buenos Aires.
"Why don't they jail corrupt politicians and murderous soldiers instead?" shouted Sivori as she was taken inside.
As one of Latin America's most wanted men, Gorriaran Merlo has spent half his life in hiding.

After leading a series of bloody guerrilla attacks and kidnappings in Argentina in the early 1970s, he joined Nicaragua's Sandinista rebels and was said to have carried out the assassination of the ousted Somoza in Paraguay in 1980.
Reincarnated as head of the Marxist rebel group MTP, he was blamed for masterminding the La Tablada assault to foil what he said was a military plot to overthrow elected President Raul Alfonsin.
About 20 of his MTP comrades were caught and jailed for up to 20 years. However, Gorriaran Merlo, who directed the operation at a safe distance from outside the barracks, got away.
Asked by reporters at his trial on Thursday if he had led the young MTP guerrillas to their deaths, he snapped back: I don't lead anyone by the nose; or do you think people are stupid?"
